class_year: str = Form(\"\"), role: str = Form(\"\"),\n                   password: str = Form(\"\")):\n    values = {\"email\": email, \"name\": name, \"class_year\": class_year,\n              \"role\": role}\n\n    def refuse(message: str):\n        return _form(request, account, values, message, 400)\n\n    if not email.strip() or \"@\" not in email:\n        return refuse(\"Enter an email address.\")\n    if not name.strip():\n        return refuse(\"Enter a name.\")\n    if not class_year.strip().isdigit():\n        return refuse(\"Class year must be a number, such as 2027.\")\n    if role not in ROLES:\n        return refuse(\"Role must be Admin or Editor.\")\n    if not password:\n        return refuse(\"Enter an initial password.\")\n    if accounts.create_account(email, name.strip(), int(class_year), role,\n                               password) is None:\n        return refuse(\"That email is already in use by another Account.\")\n    return _done()\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{account_id}/role\")\ndef change_role(request: Request, account_id: int,\n                account: Account = Depends(manage), role: str = Form(\"\")):\n    if role not in ROLES:\n        return _listing(request, account, \"Role must be Admin or Editor.\", 400)\n    try:\n        accounts.set_role(account_id, role)\n    except accounts.UnknownAccount:\n        return _done()\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{account_id}/deactivate\")\ndef deactivate(request: Request, account_id: int,\n               account: Account = Depends(manage)):\n    try:\n        accounts.deactivate(account_id)\n    except accounts.UnknownAccount:\n        return _listing(request, account, \"No such Account.\", 404)\n    except accounts.LastActiveAdmin:\n        return _listing(request, account, LAST_ADMIN_ERROR, 400)\n    return _done()\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{account_id}/password\")\ndef set_password(request: Request, account_id: int,\n                 account: Account = Depends(manage), password: str = Form(\"\")):\n    if not password:\n        return _listing(request, account, \"Enter a new password.\", 400)\n    try:\n        accounts.set_password(account_id, password)\n    except accounts.UnknownAccount:\n        return _listing(request, account, \"No such Account.\", 404)\n    return {"parentUuid":"4ea3475a-4a0b-4104-9cc8-4092be287256","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c7a459a9-6157-4be7-b976-ecdee4c5da61","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"7b2a3cf5-5725-4d8e-8829-f297e8c74d2b","timestamp":"2026-10-24T15:17:00.065Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"75c13c6b-9b63-4033-a5e2-56d95f7ba4db","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"75c13c6b-9b63-4033-a5e2-56d95f7ba4db","hash":"8e2977aee8c9d7d11644fe59b11605a1264195c43738d7772313a8787a784567","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>code-review</command-message>\n<command-name>/code-review</command-name>\n"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]}}

Verdict: no hard violations of the CLAUDE.md constraints. The items below are judgement calls except where marked.\n  \n  **Hard constraints checked, all pass**\n  - CSRF: all 5 forms (sign-out, role, password, deactivate, new Account) carry `csrf_token`. The tests cover missing and bad tokens for every POST.\n  - Passwords: they are hashed with argon2 through the existing `hash_password`. Nothing logs or stores a plain password, and the tests check for the `$argon2` prefix.\n  - Relative paths: the admin templates use absolute `/admin/...` and `/logout` paths. That only breaks the \"relative only\" rule for published HTML. `site/` is not touched, so it is fine.\n  - Access control: routes use `require(\"accounts.manage\")`, which is Admin-only. Rows were added to `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES`, as the comment in test_t01.py asks later tickets to do.\n  - Vocabulary: Deactivate, Account, Admin and Editor are used correctly, and there is no Reactivate. Two small slips are listed under \"Standards nits\".\n  \n  **Standards nits (documented, minor)**\n  1. `app/routes/accounts.py` imports `policy` and uses `policy.ADMIN` and `policy.EDITOR`. This matches `policy.py`, so it is fine. `ROLES` is a tuple of those two names.\n  2. `templates/admin/accounts.html` and `account_new.html` print the raw `a.role` (\"admin\", \"editor\") in the role dropdown and the table. CONTEXT.md capitalizes the terms Admin and Editor, so the user-facing text should arguably be \"Admin\" and \"Editor\". The Role cell and the `<option>` text are the places.\n  3. The `_header.html` string \"New Account\" is correct. The CONTEXT.md \"Avoid: User\" rule is respected.\n  \n  **Scope**\n  - `tests/test_t01.py` is edited, but only to fill `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES`, which its own comment says each ticket should do. This is within the \"no edits beyond what the ticket needs\" rule.\n  - `templates/admin/_header.html` is a new shared file. `hello.html` still holds the identical inline sign-out form, which the diff leaves alone.\n  \n  **Smells (judgement calls)**\n  - **Duplicated Code:** the `try/except UnknownAccount/LastActiveAdmin` cascade is repeated in `change_role` and `deactivate`. `except accounts.UnknownAccount: return _listing(request, account, \"No such Account.\", 404)` appears 3 times, and `LAST_ADMIN_ERROR` is returned in 2 places. A shared helper or a shared exception-to-response mapping would remove this (this is also Repeated Switches). `_listing` and `_form` have the same shape too.\n  - **Duplicated Code (template):** the header block in `hello.html` duplicates `_header.html`. T02 introduced the include and did not use it for hello.html, which would be one more edit outside the ticket.\n  - **Duplicated Code (SQL/logic):** `list_accounts` and `get` repeat `SELECT * FROM account` and `from_row`. That is mild.\n  - **Primitive Obsession:** `role: str` and `class_year: str` are bare strings. `ROLES` plus `role not in ROLES` is checked in both `create_account` and `change_role` in the routes. `accounts.set_role` does no validation itself, so the model layer trusts its caller.\n  - **Data Clumps:** `values` dict (`email`, `name`, `class_year`, `role`) is the same group as the `create_account` parameters (`email`, `name`, `class_year`, `role`, `password`). `_form` and `_listing` each take `(request, account, ...)`.\n  - **Mysterious Name:** `_done()` returns a redirect to the list, so a name like `_back_to_list` would be clearer. `_form` is vague next to `_listing`; `new_account_form` fits better. `account_new.html` is named \"new\" while the title is \"New Account\", fine.\n  - **Divergent Change (mild):** `app/routes/accounts.py` mixes input validation (create_account has a 5-step if-cascade), error wording, and routing.\n  - **Feature Envy:** none worth noting. `_lock_account` and `_is_last_active_admin` take a `conn` and a raw `row` and reach into `row[\"role\"]` and `row[\"active\"]` instead of using `Account`, which is a small leak of the row shape.\n  - **Speculative Generality:** none. `status_code` and `error` parameters are all used.\n</agent-message>"}

The CSRF check runs before the id check, which is correct.\n  - **Session handling.** `current_account` rereads the Account on every request, so role changes and Deactivation apply at once. The promotion, demotion and existing-session tests exercise this properly.\n  - **Editor table is not vacuous.** `test_editor_on_admin_only_routes` sends a valid CSRF token, so the 403 comes from the permission check and not from CSRF. It accepts 302, 303 or 403, and an Editor would get 403 here.\n  - **Unused parameter.** `set_password` calls `_lock_account` and ignores its return value. This is harmless.\n  - **Passwords.** No minimum length is enforced. The ticket doesn't ask for one.\n  \n  Files: `app/accounts.py`, `app/routes/accounts.py`, `tests/test_t02.py`.\n</agent-message>"}

superscript two: isdigit() but not int()\n    \"\\u0662\\u0660\\u0662\\u0667\",      # Arabic-Indic 2027: not ASCII digits\n    \"99999999999999999999\",          # overflows SQLite\n    \"0\", \"1999\", \"2101\", \"20277\", \"-2027\", \"202.7\", \" \",\n])\ndef test_class_year_must_be_a_four_digit_year_2000_to_2100(client_as, class_year):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    before = account_count()\n    r = create(admin, class_year=class_year)\n    assert r.status_code == 400\n    assert \"class year\" in r.text.lower() and \"2000\" in r.text\n    assert account_count() == before\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"class_year\", [\"2000\", \"2027\", \"2100\"])\ndef test_class_year_boundaries_are_accepted(client_as, class_year):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert create(admin, class_year=class_year).status_code == 303\n    assert accounts.get(account_id(NEW_ACCOUNT[\"email\"])).class_year == int(class_year)\n\n\ndef test_roles_are_shown_capitalized(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    listing = admin.get(LIST).text\n    assert \"<td>Admin</td>\" in listing and \"<td>Editor</td>\" in listing\n    assert \"<td>admin</td>\" not in listing and \"<td>editor</td>\" not in listing\n    for page in (listing, admin.get(NEW_FORM).text):\n        assert \">Admin</option>\" in page and \">Editor</option>\" in page\n        assert \">admin</option>\" not in page and \">editor</option>\" not in page\n        assert 'value=\"admin\"' in page and 'value=\"editor\"' in page  # wire values\n\n\ndef test_an_admin_deactivating_themselves_loses_their_own_session(client_as):\n    \"\"\"Allowed while another Admin is active; the redirect is their last page.\"\"\"\n    me = client_as(\"admin\")\n    my_id = account_id(DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"])\n    second_id = make_second_admin()\n    assert post(me, f\"{LIST}/{my_id}/deactivate\").status_code == 303\n    assert not accounts.get(my_id).active\n    assert accounts.get(second_id).active\n    after = me.get(LIST, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert after.status_code == 303 and after.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n    _, login = signed_in(DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n                         DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"])\n    assert login.status_code == 401\n\n\ndef test_an_admin_demoting_themselves_loses_admin_pages_but_stays_signed_in(client_as):\n    me = client_as(\"admin\")\n    my_id = account_id(DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"])\n    make_second_admin()\n    assert post(me, f\"{LIST}/{my_id}/role\", role=\"editor\").status_code == 303\n    assert me.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n    assert me.get(LIST, follow_redirects=False).status_code == 403\nEOF\nuv run pytest tests/test_t02.py -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 | tail -40","description":"Add follow-up tests and run them before fixing"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

Standards and Spec reviewers ran separately. After fixes: `uv run pytest -q` gives 97 passed, 0 skipped (T01's skip, the empty Editor-on-Admin-only table, is now filled in).\n\n### Standards\nNo hard violations of CLAUDE.md or SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md (CSRF on every form, argon2 only, no plain password stored or logged, every route behind `accounts.manage`).\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Roles shown as lowercase `admin` / `editor`; CONTEXT.md capitalizes Admin and Editor | **Fixed.** Role cells, dropdown labels and the header show Admin / Editor (form values stay lowercase). Test added. |\n| Duplicated error handling (`UnknownAccount` / `LastActiveAdmin`) across routes; `_listing` and `_form` share a shape | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Mysterious Name: `_done`, `_form` | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Primitive Obsession: role and class year as strings; `accounts.set_role` does not validate | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Data Clumps: form `values` vs `create_account` parameters | Left as a judgement call. |\n| `hello.html` sign-out form duplicates `_header.html` | Left as a judgement call (editing `hello.html` is outside this ticket). |\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Class year: `\"²\".isdigit()` is true but `int()` raises, giving a 500; a huge number overflows SQLite (500); `0` accepted | **Fixed test-first.** Ten failing tests written first (superscript, Arabic-Indic digits, huge number, 0, 1999, 2101, 20277, negative, decimal, blank). Class year must now be four ASCII digits between 2000 and 2100, otherwise a 400 with a clear message. Boundary tests (2000, 2027, 2100) added. |\n| Admin deactivating or demoting themselves while another Admin is active is untested | **Fixed.** Two tests document the behavior: a self-Deactivated Admin loses their session at once, and a self-demoted Admin stays signed in but gets 403 on Accounts pages. |\n| Non-integer account id (422) untested | **Deferred to T03.** |\n| \"Recaps, Pages and Bylines stay as they are\" cannot be tested yet | **Deferred to T03**, which adds those tables. `test_deactivating_keeps_the_account_row` is the proxy for now. |\n| Role and password changes on a Deactivated Account still work via a direct POST | Left as is: harmless, the ticket is silent. Next I'll post the findings and resolutions to issue #3."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Grg8q7ycTefD4eRBcZiepE","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && F=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrewv-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/75c13c6b-9b63-4033-a5e2-56d95f7ba4db/scratchpad/t02-review.md && cat > $F <<'EOF'\n## T02 `/code-review` findings and resolutions\n\nReviewed the uncommitted T02 working tree against `HEAD` (dd7c174). Standards and Spec reviewers ran separately. After fixes: `uv run pytest -q` gives 97 passed, 0 skipped (T01's skip, the empty Editor-on-Admin-only table, is now filled in).\n\n### Standards\nNo hard violations of CLAUDE.md or SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md (CSRF on every form, argon2 only, no plain password stored or logged, every route behind `accounts.manage`).\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Roles shown as lowercase `admin` / `editor`; CONTEXT.md capitalizes Admin and Editor | **Fixed.** Role cells, dropdown labels and the header show Admin / Editor (form values stay lowercase). Test added. |\n| Duplicated error handling (`UnknownAccount` / `LastActiveAdmin`) across routes; `_listing` and `_form` share a shape | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Mysterious Name: `_done`, `_form` | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Primitive Obsession: role and class year as strings; `accounts.set_role` does not validate | Left as a judgement call. |\n| Data Clumps: form `values` vs `create_account` parameters | Left as a judgement call. |\n| `hello.html` sign-out form duplicates `_header.html` | Left as a judgement call (editing `hello.html` is outside this ticket). |\n\n### Spec\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Class year: `\"²\".isdigit()` is true but `int()` raises, giving a 500; a huge number overflows SQLite (500); `0` accepted | **Fixed test-first.** Ten failing tests written first (superscript, Arabic-Indic digits, huge number, 0, 1999, 2101, 20277, negative, decimal, blank). Class year must now be four ASCII digits between 2000 and 2100, otherwise a 400 with a clear message. Boundary tests (2000, 2027, 2100) added. |\n| Admin deactivating or demoting themselves while another Admin is active is untested | **Fixed.** Two tests document the behavior: a self-Deactivated Admin loses their session at once, and a self-demoted Admin stays signed in but gets 403 on Accounts pages. |\n| Non-integer account id (422) untested | **Deferred to T03.** |\n| \"Recaps, Pages and Bylines stay as they are\" cannot be tested yet | **Deferred to T03**, which adds those tables. `test_deactivating_keeps_the_account_row` is the proxy for now. |\n| Role and password changes on a Deactivated Account still work via a direct POST | Left as is: harmless, the ticket is silent. A test confirms it never reactivates. |\n| Nav bar in `_header.html`; ordering in `list_accounts` | Left as is: minor UI, not in the ticket. |\n| Email check only looks for `@`; `set_password` ignores `_lock_account`'s return value | Left as judgement calls. |\n| Concurrent last-Admin race untested | Not changed: `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` covers it. |\nEOF\ngh issue comment 3 --body-file $F","description":"Post review findings comment on issue 3"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}
